prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1498; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change. Insured reports the other vehicle merged into their lane without signaling. Both drivers reported no visible damage beyond right-side panel scrapes. Police report requested. Recorded statement from insured taken and scheduled for file.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Letter of representation received. All further contact to go through the attorney's office. Claimant reports neck strain and is seeking medical evaluation. Medical authorization forms sent to counsel for signature.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received from insured and claimant's side. Damage estimate completed for insured vehicle at the right rear quarter panel and mirror assembly. Adjuster noted the claimant vehicle shows damage to the left front bumper area, consistent with the reported lane-change contact. Liability review in progress.

Entry 4: Attorney's office provided initial treatment records indicating diagnosis of cervical strain with prescribed physical therapy. Demand package not yet received. Reserve adjusted to reflect possible bodily injury exposure. Supervisor notified of represented claim with injury component.

Entry 5: Liability analysis reviewed. Available evidence supports the other driver as primarily at fault for the lane change. Awaiting police report and final medical records before evaluating settlement posture. Follow-up scheduled with claimant's counsel to confirm treatment status and request updated billing.
